story: Southcentral Alaska enters the 2026-27 heating season about 3 Bcf below its ideal gas storage level. Enstar says any reductions are phased by customer class under its tariff, and the only public account of where large commercial and industrial load sits in that order is a mayor relaying what the utility told a room of mayors.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet Gas Watch measured Cook Inlet storage inventory at 7,648,351 Mcf on September 10th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: "inventory_mcf":7648351
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: Read from the last committed record in ledger/gaswatch.jsonl, collected 2026-09-10T17:16:41Z with CINGSA source timestamp 2026-09-10T09:00:00 local. The underlying dashboard is CINGSA's, at https://cingsa.com/operations/PublicDashBoard.html, and CINGSA keeps no archive, so this series exists only because it is collected daily. This record supersedes an earlier same day posting at 01:02:00.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet Gas Watch page publishes that September 10th, 2026 reading as 7.65 of 13.0 Bcf.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: 7,648,351 Mcf rounds to 7.65 Bcf, so the Bcf rendering and the Mcf ledger value agree. Use one or the other on a slide, never both as if they were two facts.

claims.claim: CINGSA's storage design capacity as recorded by the Cook Inlet Gas Watch is 13,000,000 Mcf, published as 13.0 Bcf.
claims.verbatim: "storage_design_mcf":13000000
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: Design volume of the field, read from the CINGSA public dashboard. It is a design figure and not a measure of what is deliverable on any given day.

claims.claim: Cook Inlet storage stood at 58.8 percent of design volume on September 10th, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: Matches inventory_pct_of_design in the ledger record. This is a measurement of one field on one day and is not a verdict about winter adequacy. The page publishes no safety verdict, so no slide may turn this percentage into one.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet Gas Watch demand model in force on September 10th, 2026 is version 2.0.
claims.verbatim: Version 2.0
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: Carried per record in the ledger so an old number stays reproducible.

claims.claim: The published demand model states that regional demand in MMcf per day equals 80.868 plus 3.439 times heating degree days on a base of 65 Fahrenheit.
claims.verbatim: Regional demand in MMcf per day is 80.868 plus 3.439 times heating degree days, base 65 Fahrenheit
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: Fitted by least squares against 131 months of observed EIA Alaska deliveries to residential, commercial and electric power consumers. Demand is MODELED, not measured, and any slide printing it must say so.

claims.claim: The highest modeled demand in the Cook Inlet Gas Watch forecast window as of September 10th, 2026 is 120 MMcf per day.
claims.verbatim: 120 MMcf/d modeled peak ahead
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: Peak falls on September 16th, 2026 at 11.3 heating degree days. This is model output and not a measurement. It is a September number in mild weather and can't be presented as a winter peak.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet Gas Watch holds 36 days on record as of September 10th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: 36 days on record
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: The page's JSON-LD gives temporalCoverage 2026-08-05/2026-09-10 and distributionSize 36. The raw ledger holds 86 lines because some days carry a superseded earlier posting, so line count is not day count. Do not print 86.

claims.claim: Of the 36 days on record, 2 carry no verified reading because a fetch failed or the source had stopped updating.
claims.verbatim: Of 36 days on record, 2 carry no verified reading because a fetch failed or the source had stopped updating
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: 34 of 36 days verified. This is the publication disclosing its own gaps, which is the strongest honesty beat available to the deck. A failed fetch carries no number forward from the previous day.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet Gas Watch publishes 63.7 days of cover at modeled peak and states in the same field that it is not a measure of adequacy.
claims.verbatim: Inventory divided by modeled peak demand. It is arithmetic on storage alone and takes no account of the withdrawal capacity ceiling, field supply, or deliverability. It is not a measure of adequacy.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: HARD HEDGE. If the deck prints 63.7, it must print the disclaimer with it on the same slide. Printing the number alone would be a shortfall forecast, which this publication's rules forbid.

claims.claim: CINGSA's published operating withdrawal capacity on September 10th, 2026 was 150,000 Mcf per day against a design figure of 215,000 Mcf per day.
claims.verbatim: "withdrawal_design_mcfd":215000,"withdrawal_facility_mcfd":166000,"withdrawal_operating_mcfd":150000
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: The record flags cingsa_capacity_identity_mismatch because facility capacity less physical restriction does not equal published operating capacity on either stream. Useful because storage volume is not the binding constraint, deliverability is.

claims.claim: CINGSA posted that it will perform a required semiannual shut in field balance and maintenance from September 14th to September 21st, 2026 and will accept no nominations during that time.
claims.verbatim: CINGSA will be performing required semiannual shut-in field balance & maintenance from 14; Sept. 2026 until 21 Sept. 2026. No nominations will be accepted during this time.
claims.source_outlet: CINGSA public dashboard, captured by Alaska AI Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: Captured verbatim into the operational_note field of the September 10th record, including CINGSA's own punctuation error. The same note says Compressor B is down for needed maintenance affecting initial and legacy injection customers only. The dashboard is live and unarchived, so the Gas Watch capture is the citable copy.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet Gas Watch derived non CINGSA supply of 138.3 MMcf per day for September 9th, 2026 from its mass balance.
claims.verbatim: "non_cingsa_supply_mmcfd":138.3
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: Derived, not measured. It is modeled demand less the measured CINGSA inventory draw, so it combines field production with any Hilcorp storage movement and is never called production. The page states this figure is published nowhere else.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet Gas Watch states it publishes no safety verdict.
claims.verbatim: No safety verdict, ever.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska AI, Cook Inlet Gas Watch
claims.notes: From the page's own description metadata. The dataset description repeats it as publishing no safety verdict, no shortfall prediction and no all clear. This claim exists so the deck can print its own limit on a slide.

claims.claim: Enstar president John Sims told state lawmakers in August that Enstar was about 3 billion cubic feet short of its ideal storage level heading into the coming heating season.
claims.verbatim: Sims separately told state lawmakers in August that Enstar was about 3 billion cubic feet short of its ideal storage level heading into the coming heating season.
claims.notes: ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION. The 3 Bcf figure was NOT given at a Kenai Peninsula meeting. Homer News attributes it to Sims speaking to state lawmakers in August. Peninsula Clarion carries the same article, same byline Jeffrey Kennett, same chain, and is NOT an independent second source.

claims.claim: Kenai Mayor Henry Knackstedt told the Kenai City Council on September 2nd, 2026 that Enstar president John Sims recently put the storage deficit at the equivalent of about 18 days of winter demand if temperatures are normal or slightly colder.
claims.verbatim: Kenai Mayor Henry Knackstedt told the City Council on Wednesday, Sept. 2 that Enstar President John Sims recently put the deficit at the equivalent of about 18 days of winter demand if temperatures are normal or slightly colder.
claims.notes: Second hand. A newspaper reporting a mayor relaying what a utility president said. Do not write Enstar says 18 days flat. The conditional if temperatures are normal or slightly colder is part of the figure and can't be dropped.

claims.claim: Enstar communications manager Harley Hedlund said the deficit figure does not mean the utility will be short that many days this winter.
claims.value: This doesn't mean we will be short this many days this winter.
claims.verbatim: This doesn't mean we will be short this many days this winter. Rather, it demonstrates how tight the situation is and our reduced resources to respond to unexpected events.
claims.notes: Confirmed character for character across two separate fetches. THIS IS THE DECK'S SHIELD. It is the utility itself refusing to turn 18 days into a shortage forecast. If the deck prints the 18 days figure anywhere, this quote should appear on the same slide or the next one.

claims.claim: Harley Hedlund is Enstar's communications manager.
claims.verbatim: Enstar Communications Manager
claims.notes: Title confirmed on the page. Not independently confirmed against an Enstar staff page.

claims.claim: Kenai Mayor Henry Knackstedt said Enstar described a plan that would first look to large commercial and industrial users for reductions before residential customers.
claims.value: large commercial and industrial users before residential customers
claims.verbatim: He said Enstar described a plan that would first look to large commercial and industrial users for reductions before residential customers.
claims.notes: THE SPINE, AND ITS LIMIT. The sequence is NOT quoted from a curtailment tariff document anyone could open. He is Mayor Knackstedt. This is a mayor's public account of what Enstar described at the August 21st mayors meeting. The deck must attribute it as such. It may NOT be captioned as tariff text. Print alongside C20 or it overclaims.

claims.claim: Enstar said any reductions would be phased by customer class under the utility's tariff, with service to facilities serving human needs and occupancy given the highest priority.
claims.value: phased by customer class under the utility's tariff
claims.verbatim: Any reductions would be phased by customer class under the utility's tariff, with service to facilities serving human needs and occupancy given the highest priority.
claims.notes: This establishes that a TARIFF exists and that phasing is by customer class. Materially stronger than C19 because it names the instrument. It does NOT itself name large commercial and industrial as the first class cut. Pair C19 and C20 and the deck is accurate.

claims.claim: Enstar said modest thermostat adjustments down to 65 degrees, where safe and practical, could help reduce demand during periods of extreme cold.
claims.verbatim: modest thermostat adjustments down to 65 degrees, where safe and practical, could help reduce demand during periods of extreme cold
claims.notes: The qualifiers modest, where safe and practical and could help are in the source and should survive onto the slide. This is the voluntary conservation step that precedes any curtailment.

claims.claim: Enstar does not now anticipate receiving gas from BlueCrest Energy's Cosmopolitan Unit until the first quarter of 2027 at the earliest, after an expected early September delivery slipped.
claims.value: first quarter of 2027 at the earliest
claims.notes: The page carries two typographical errors in this passage, so verbatim is deliberately null rather than reproducing a misspelling as a quotation. The facts are confirmed on the page.

claims.claim: Kenai Mayor Henry Knackstedt said Enstar president John Sims indicated an LNG import project using the Nikiski area may not be ready until the fourth quarter of 2029.
claims.verbatim: Knackstedt said Sims indicated an import project using the Nikiski area may not be ready until the fourth quarter of 2029.
claims.notes: Double hedged in the source itself. Knackstedt said Sims INDICATED it MAY not be ready. Write it as reportedly not before late 2029 and attribute to Knackstedt.

claims.claim: Kenai Mayor Henry Knackstedt met with Enstar president John Sims and other Southcentral mayors on August 21st, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Knackstedt met with Sims and other Southcentral mayors Aug. 21.
claims.notes: This is the setting for C19. The meeting is a mayors meeting, not a Kenai Peninsula public meeting.

claims.claim: Enstar was in emergency arbitration with HEX Operating over access to additional gas beyond what the producer was already delivering under contract.
claims.verbatim: Enstar was in emergency arbitration with HEX Operating over access to additional gas beyond what the producer was already delivering under contract.
claims.notes: SINGLE SOURCED and absent from four other reports checked. Ship only with Homer News reported attribution, or keep as background.

claims.claim: Enstar communications manager Harley Hedlund said executed gas sharing agreements with Matanuska Electric Association and Chugach Electric Association would not be filed with the Regulatory Commission of Alaska.
claims.value: would not be filed with the Regulatory Commission of Alaska
claims.verbatim: Hedlund said executed agreements would not be filed with the Regulatory Commission of Alaska.
claims.notes: SINGLE SOURCED. The companion sentence says Enstar has EXPLORED arrangements, not signed them. Write Enstar told Homer News that any executed agreements would not be filed with the RCA, and do not assert the RCA agrees or that this is unlawful.

claims.claim: Alaskans use about 70 billion cubic feet of natural gas from Cook Inlet each year on average.
claims.value: about 70 billion cubic feet a year
claims.verbatim: On average, Alaskans use about 70 billion cubic feet of natural gas from Cook Inlet each year.
claims.notes: The source says Alaskans statewide, not Southcentral only, so do not relabel it as a Southcentral figure.

claims.claim: Southcentral Alaska relies on natural gas for more than 70 percent of its electricity.
claims.verbatim: more than 70% of its electricity
claims.notes: The article attributes the figure to the Institute of Social and Economic Research. Attribute on the slide as Alaska Public Media citing ISER.

claims.claim: Enstar sells gas to almost half of Alaska's population and gets nearly all of its supply from Hilcorp.
claims.verbatim: sells gas to almost half of Alaska's population
claims.notes: Second verbatim on the same page is gets nearly all of its supply from Hilcorp. This REPLACES the killed claim of more than 150,000 Enstar customers. Single supplier concentration is the point worth making.

claims.claim: Enstar is currently paying close to 11 dollars per mcf of natural gas.
claims.verbatim: currently paying close to $11 per mcf of natural gas
claims.notes: Hedge word close to is in the source and should survive. This is a delivered utility cost, not a wellhead price.

claims.claim: The Japan Korea spot market for LNG is trading at 24 dollars, more than double Enstar's current rate.
claims.verbatim: is trading at $24
claims.notes: UNITS HEDGE. JKM is conventionally quoted per MMBtu, close to but not identical with per mcf. Write about $24 on the Japan Korea spot market, according to Alaska Public Media, and do not stamp per mcf onto the $24 as though the source did.

claims.claim: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska issued its order denying Enstar's request for an advance determination of prudence on July 8th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: July 8, 2026
claims.notes: DATE PINNED. July 10th is the ADN publication date, not the order date. ADN's own text says the commission acted on Wednesday, which was July 8th. Two outlets in different chains agree. Background, outside the run window.

claims.claim: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska wrote that an advance determination of prudence is an extraordinary request not explicitly contemplated in its governing statutes or regulations.
claims.value: an extraordinary request not explicitly contemplated
claims.verbatim: An advance determination of prudence is an extraordinary request not explicitly contemplated in our governing statutes or regulations
claims.notes: The RCA's own words as quoted by Petroleum News. rca.alaska.gov returns 403 to automated requests, so this is a quotation of a primary document rather than the document. Attribute as the commission wrote, as quoted by Petroleum News.

claims.claim: Enstar filed a 31 page petition for reconsideration of the commission's denial.
claims.verbatim: 31-page petition
claims.notes: Page count is solid. The filing DATE is not pinned and does not ship. KTOO and alaskapublic.org are the SAME story by the SAME author and count as ONE source.

claims.claim: Enstar told the commission in its original filing that the proposed storage facility would cost 240 million dollars and add up to 12 dollars a month to the average customer bill.
claims.verbatim: Enstar had said in its original filing to the commission that the proposed facility would cost $240 million, and add up to $12 a month to the average customer bill.
claims.notes: By Alex DeMarban. Corroborated at $240 million by Petroleum News and Alaska Public Media, three separate chains. The $12 a month figure appears only in ADN and is the more useful half for a general reader.

claims.claim: The storage project is described as the largest single capital investment in Enstar's history.
claims.value: largest single capital investment in the utility's history
claims.verbatim: the largest single capital investment in the utility's history
claims.notes: The outlet's characterisation. Keep the passive attribution, described as.

claims.claim: Enstar president John Sims said the reservoir is almost perfect for what Enstar views as short term and long term needs.
claims.value: almost perfect for what Enstar views as short term and long term needs
claims.verbatim: This reservoir is almost perfect for what Enstar views as short term and long term needs,
claims.notes: Background, outside the run window.

claims.claim: Enstar president John Sims said there is a lot of planning going on for the upcoming winter about what happens if there is a gas supply issue, because the utility is worried.
claims.value: There's a lot of planning going on for this upcoming winter
claims.verbatim: There's a lot of planning going on for this upcoming winter about what happens if we have a gas supply issue, because we're worried
claims.notes: The utility characterising its own posture, which keeps the deck out of forecasting. From July 2026, so label as background if used.

claims.claim: Enstar's petition for an advance determination of decisional prudence for the natural gas storage project is docket U-26-003 and Enstar publishes the filing itself on its own regulatory filings page.
claims.verbatim: U-26-003 - ENSTAR Petition for Advance Determination of Decisional Prudence (Natural Gas Storage Project)
claims.notes: PRIMARY. The company's own current regulatory filings page, fetched today. The linked petition PDF exceeded a 10 MB fetch limit, so the docket number and title are confirmed but not the text inside. The page lists TA353-4, TA354-4 and TA360-4 and lists NO petition for reconsideration and NO arbitration filing.

claims.claim: Enstar's approved tariff contains a section numbered 1200 titled Interruption, published on Enstar's own tariff information page.
claims.verbatim: Section 1200 - Interruption
claims.notes: PRIMARY for the EXISTENCE of the tariff section, NOT for its contents. The Section 1200 PDF returned as a 2.4 MB binary that would not extract to text and no page renderer was available. The tariff page also lists Section 1600 Transportation Service and Section 2200 Large Transportation Interruptible. Do not caption a slide as if the tariff was read.

claims.claim: Golden Valley Electric Association's overall residential rate drops to 34.55 cents per kilowatt hour and is still the highest on the Railbelt.
claims.verbatim: The overall drop to 34.55 cents per kilowatt-hour is still the highest on the Railbelt
claims.notes: By Jack Barnwell. This is a RESIDENTIAL rate and the five cents figure in C45 is an INDUSTRIAL one, so the deck must not present them as the same measure.

claims.claim: The reduction lowers Golden Valley Electric Association's fuel and purchased power rate by 2.6 cents per kilowatt hour to 18.049 cents.
claims.verbatim: The reduction lowers GVEA's fuel/powered purchase rate by 2.6 cents per kilowatt-hour to 18.049 cents.
claims.notes: 18.049 cents of fuel and purchased power inside a 34.55 cent all in residential rate is 52 percent of the bill, a coherent magnitude for a fuel heavy Railbelt utility.

claims.claim: Golden Valley Electric Association residential rates will drop by 12.6 percent, or 15 dollars a month for the average household.
claims.verbatim: Golden Valley Electric Association residential rates will drop by 12.6%, or $15 a month for the average household
claims.notes: Cuts against a one sided framing. Railbelt power is expensive AND it just fell. Carry this if the deck carries C41.

claims.claim: The Alaska Gasline Development Corporation plans to seek 2.5 million dollars from state lawmakers for a program enabling Alaskans to invest directly in the Alaska LNG pipeline project.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News, reporting by Alaska Beacon
claims.notes: By James Brooks of Alaska Beacon, describing an AGDC board meeting on September 3rd, 2026. The figure is the reporter's statement attributed to AGDC president Frank Richards and is reported, not quoted. Write AGDC said it will ask the Legislature for about $2.5 million, according to the Alaska Beacon.

claims.claim: Broadband Breakfast reported that Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy said the state is advancing a natural gas pipeline that could deliver power at about five cents per kilowatt hour for industrial users.
claims.value: about five cents per kilowatt hour
claims.verbatim: The state is advancing a natural gas pipeline that could deliver power at about five cents per kilowatt hour for industrial users
claims.notes: PARTIAL KILL. The five cents line is the OUTLET'S PARAPHRASE of Dunleavy's remarks at Data Center World, NOT a direct quotation. It may NOT be set in quotation marks and attributed to Dunleavy as his words. Ships only as Broadband Breakfast reported that Dunleavy said, with the hedge could deliver intact, and only as clearly labelled background. It is a FUTURE price off a pipeline that does not exist.

stories_surviving: Southcentral gas storage enters winter about 3 Bcf below ideal and Enstar says any cuts are phased by customer class under its tariff
The Cook Inlet Gas Watch daily measurement, 7.65 of 13.0 Bcf at 58.8 percent of design on September 10th, 2026, with 34 of 36 days verified
Relief supply is years out, BlueCrest Cosmopolitan no earlier than the first quarter of 2027 and a Nikiski import project possibly not before the fourth quarter of 2029
The regulatory record behind the missing storage, the RCA's July 8th, 2026 denial in docket U-26-003 and Enstar's 31 page petition for reconsideration
What Railbelt power actually costs, GVEA at 34.55 cents per kilowatt hour against a five cents industrial promise that depends on a pipeline

killed.claim: More than 150,000 Enstar customers are supplied almost entirely by Hilcorp.
killed.why: The customer count does not appear on the page cited for it. Replaced by C29. Do not print 150,000.

killed.claim: Gov. Mike Dunleavy said, in quotation marks, five cents per kilowatt hour for industrial users.
killed.why: Those words are Broadband Breakfast's paraphrase, not a direct quotation. Survives only in the attributed paraphrase form recorded as C45.

killed.claim: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska denied Enstar's advance determination of prudence on July 10th, 2026.
killed.why: July 10th is the ADN publication date. The order date is July 8th, 2026. Corrected as C32.

killed.claim: Enstar told a Kenai Peninsula meeting that storage is roughly 3 Bcf below ideal.
killed.why: Wrong venue. The 3 Bcf figure went to state lawmakers in August, the 18 days figure came from Mayor Knackstedt at a September 2nd Kenai City Council meeting, and the mayors meeting on August 21st is a third separate event. Split into C15, C16 and C24.

killed.claim: Enstar's published curtailment tariff sets the sequence as conservation, then large commercial and industrial, then residential.
killed.why: No tariff text supports this as fetched. Section 1200 Interruption exists but the PDF would not extract. The ordering rests on Mayor Knackstedt's account, C19. The tariff based statement that survives is the weaker and accurate C20.

killed.claim: Enstar's petition for reconsideration was filed on July 23rd or July 24th, 2026.
killed.why: Not pinned. Both pages say only Thursday. No filing date ships. The 31 page count survives as C34.

killed.claim: Peninsula Clarion independently corroborates the Homer News reporting.
killed.why: Same chain, same byline, same article. One source, not two.

killed.claim: Enstar is negotiating signed inter utility gas sharing arrangements with Matanuska Electric and Chugach Electric.
killed.why: Overstated. The source says Enstar has EXPLORED arrangements that COULD make gas available. The surviving softened version is C26.
